subsystems.name: Holder wallet
subsystems.role: stores the user's decentralized identifiers, private keys and verifiable credentials, and presents proofs to verifiers.

subsystems.name: Issuer service
subsystems.role: verifies a subject's attributes and issues signed verifiable credentials to their wallet.

subsystems.name: Verifier service
subsystems.role: requests specific credentials or claims from a holder and checks their authenticity and validity.

subsystems.name: DID method and resolver
subsystems.role: defines how a decentralized identifier is created, resolved to a DID document, updated and deactivated.

subsystems.name: Verifiable data registry
subsystems.role: provides a shared, tamper-evident source of DID documents and credential revocation status.

subsystems.name: Cryptographic library
subsystems.role: implements key generation, digital signatures, encryption and optional zero-knowledge proofs.

buildSteps.title: Choose a DID method
buildSteps.detail: Select or define a method that specifies the identifier format, the registry it uses, and the operations for create, read, update and deactivate.

buildSteps.title: Set up the verifiable data registry
buildSteps.detail: Deploy a distributed ledger, federated ledger, or other tamper-evident store where DID documents and revocation lists can be anchored.

buildSteps.title: Implement the DID resolver and registrar
buildSteps.detail: Write software that registers new DIDs and resolves existing DIDs to their current public keys and service endpoints.

buildSteps.title: Build the holder wallet
buildSteps.detail: Create an app with secure key storage (using a secure element or trusted execution environment), credential storage, and a user interface for consent and presentation.

buildSteps.title: Implement the issuer service
buildSteps.detail: Develop APIs for credential offers and issuance, integrate a signing module that signs credentials with the issuer's private key, and connect to a revocation mechanism.

buildSteps.title: Implement the verifier service
buildSteps.detail: Build endpoints that generate presentation requests, verify signatures and proofs, check revocation status, and apply trust policies.

buildSteps.title: Establish trust and governance
buildSteps.detail: Define who is authorized to issue which credentials, how keys are recovered, how disputes are resolved, and what legal recognition the credentials have.

buildSteps.title: Test interoperability
buildSteps.detail: Run conformance tests and cross-implementation trials with other wallets, issuers and verifiers to ensure the standards work end to end.

buildSteps.title: Pilot and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Start with a limited use case such as a digital passport or health credential, gather feedback, then expand to more issuers and verifiers.

prerequisites.tech: W3C decentralized identifier (DID) and verifiable credential (VC) standards
prerequisites.why: they provide the common data model and protocols that let independent wallets and services interoperate.

prerequisites.tech: Public key cryptography and digital signatures
prerequisites.why: they let issuers sign credentials and holders prove control of their identifiers without a central authority.

prerequisites.tech: Secure hardware on user devices (secure element or trusted execution environment)
prerequisites.why: private keys must be protected from theft or misuse, especially on smartphones.

prerequisites.tech: Verifiable data registry (distributed ledger or alternative)
prerequisites.why: DIDs need a resolvable, tamper-evident registry, but no single registry is yet universally accepted or scaled.
trust in issuers, liability for misuse, and cross-border recognition must be settled before wide adoption.
they enable privacy-preserving proofs, but are computationally heavy and not yet standardized across all wallets.

pathway.milestone: government and industry pilots, such as the EU Digital Identity Wallet initiative and various health and travel credential trials
pathway.unlocks: real-world testing of wallets, issuers and verifiers with real users.

pathway.milestone: cross-border and cross-sector interoperability through standards bodies and industry consortia
pathway.unlocks: credentials issued in one jurisdiction can be verified in another.

pathway.milestone: integration with existing identity providers and enterprise systems in hybrid models
pathway.unlocks: organisations can adopt SSI gradually without replacing all legacy infrastructure.

pathway.milestone: widespread adoption for digital passports, healthcare, education and finance
pathway.unlocks: individuals control their own identity data across many services, reducing centralised data breaches.
